sentences.text:
S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous (Petition) No. 5340/2024 Ram Singh Deora S/o Shri Anoop Singh Deora, Aged About 47 Years, R/o 1-B-470 Kudi Bhagtasani Housing Board, Jodhpur.
 ----Accused-Petitioner  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through PP 2.

Bhagwat Singh Deora S/o Pratap Singh Deora, R/o B-21,
 Bhan Nagar, Queens Road, Jaipur.

----Complainant-Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Manoj Bohra For Respondent(s) : Mr. Rishi Raj Singh Rathore, P.P.
 Mr. Manvendra Singh Shekhawat, P.P.
For Complainant : Mr. Saurabh Bhagwati  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SAMEER JAIN  Judgment 09/05/2025 1.

The present petition is filed for quashing of FIR No.144/2024 dated 29.03.2024 registered at Police Station Chitrakoot Jaipur (West) for offences under sections 420, 406 and 120-B of IPC.
2.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the impugned FIR is per se illegal and is made to be registered in wrongful exercise of jurisdiction giving a color of criminal proceedings.
Learned counsel has further submitted that the FIR so lodged is bared by the principle of delay and laches as the same is made to be registered after a lapse of two years.
3. It is submitted that the partnership in question was entered in the year, 2022, the cause of action arose in the year, 2022 and FIR was lodged in the year, 2024.

It is submitted that the [2025:RJ-JP:19743] (2 of 4) [CRLMP-5340/2024] partnership agreement makes it unambiguous Ram Singh Deora S/O Shri Anoop Singh ... vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jp:19743) on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186093907/
1 that any dispute that may arose during the tenure of the partnership shall be dealt by the arbitration clause.

entities.text: Ram Singh Deora S/O Shri Anoop Singh ... vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jp:19743)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The said arbitration clause is reproduced herein below:
"All the matters of dispute or difference relating to this partnership shall be referred to Arbitration According & subject to the provision of the Arbitration Act in force for the time being.

"
4. It is further submitted that the petitioner has never availed the said arbitration clause meaning that there was no dispute.

It is further contended that the petitioner neither disputes the receipt of capital in accounts, as specified in the FIR nor disputes the fact that the said amount is lying against the capital of petitioner.
Nevertheless, the same is duly entered in the books of accounts of the partnership firm.
Therefore, qua any dispute, the foremost remedy is arbitration forum and thereafter civil suit.

Lastly, reliance is placed upon the judgment dated 16.04.2025 passed by the Apex Court in the case of Rikhab Birani and Anr. Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr., registered as S.L.P. (Crl.) No.8592 of 2024.

entities.text: Rikhab Birani and Anr. Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, learned counsel for the complainant has submitted that in blind faith qua the petitioner the complainant has given capital to run the partnership firm and subsequently the petitioner has siphoned the money in question into his personal accounts.
It is further submitted that the complainant was a sleeping partner who had invested with a guarantee return.

6. Having heard the rival arguments made by the counsel representing the respective parties, and taking note of the fact [2025:RJ-JP:19743] (3 of 4) [CRLMP-5340/2024] that the instant dispute is of civil nature; that the controversy in hand arose on account of certain monetary transactions; that in the partnership deed has a specific arbitration clause enumerated in it; that the parties herein were 50-50 per cent partners in the said partnership firm, therefore none of them can be said to be a sleeping partner; this Court deems it apposite to place reliance upon the ratio encapsulated in Rikhab Birani and Anr. (Supra) and State of Harayana and Ors. vs. Ch. Bhajan Lal and Ors.:
AIR 1992 SC 604 and is accordingly inclined to allow the present petition.

sentences.text: 7. Accordingly, the present petition is allowed.

The impugned FIR bearing no. 144/2024 dated 29.03.2024 at Police Station Chitrakoot, District Jaipur West for the offences punishable under Section 420, 406 and 120B of IPC is hereby quashed and set aside, along with all the consequential proceedings arising thereto.
Stay application, if any, shall stand disposed of.

8. Having made the observations herein above, this Court is of the view that:
In SBCRLMA No. IA 1/2025:
An application for vacating stay order dated 21.08.2024 is moved.
However, in light of the observations made hereinabove, the same stands dismissed.
